tasks.title: Dialog font-relative baseline width and shared em sizing
tasks.description:
A short confirmation dialog (Delete pane?) hugs its title/buttons and looks cramped. Provide a font-relative baseline while preserving content growth and Overlay's viewport cap.

Current scope confirmed 2026-10-24: Layout already has min/max width and height, LayoutExt builders, and taffy min_size mapping. Do not duplicate those. The missing primitive is font-relative Length support, shared by native authoring and serialized descriptions. Dialog should use a default minimum of about 22em.

Preflight:
1. Existing owners: Length parses and serializes sizes; Layout::to_taffy resolves layout values using the inherited font; LayoutEngine supplies that font. Dialog composes Flex inside Overlay; Overlay owns viewport bounds. Reuse these, with no font multiplication at app call sites. Native/plugin usage should be .min_width("22em"); serialized props use the same spelling.
2. Planner owner is this task T286. T517's separate Dialog structural cleanup is outside this sizing fix.
3. Antonio explicitly approved fixing and closing T286 and the prerequisite scoped splits: move existing Dialog tests out of its 956-line module; separate Length and layout conversion from style.rs (1727 lines), preserving public re-exports.

Implementation: add reusable font-relative lengths and native/wire parity, use a font-derived Dialog minimum, preserve the existing max viewport behavior and explicit panel sizing. No changes to pre-existing pane_header/segments.rs edits.

Verification: parser/serde round trips; length conversion for dimensions, limits, basis, insets and margins; headless Dialog layout showing short-content floor, larger-content growth, font changes, and bounded viewport behavior. Deliberately remove the fix to establish the regression test fails, then restore. Verify described trees too. Update docs/layout.md and docs/widgets.md. Run scoped cargo check/clippy/tests and the showcase; record any unverified real-window checks explicitly. No cargo fmt, commit or push.

Origin: rescued from old root HANDOFF.md section 3c (2026-07-13). The old assertion that min_width did not exist has been superseded by source verification.

---
**Completion summary:**
Shipped 2026-10-24 in /Users/antonio/projects/heca-rendering. No commit/push and no copy to /Users/antonio/projects/heca.

Shared sizing: Length::Em, CSS em parser and serde round-trip in heca-grid-ui/src/style/length.rs; font-aware dimension, min/max, flex-basis, inset and individual-margin conversion in style/layout.rs; root em margins in layout.rs. heca-view/src/build/style.rs accepts CSS lengths on SDK dimensions, limits and individual margins. Native code, JSON/config and RPC use the same Length parser; no app-side font arithmetic.

Dialog: public Dialog::BASELINE_WIDTH = 22em. Existing Flex/Overlay composition uses preferred flex basis with the content's automatic minimum. This is deliberate: a strict 22em min-width overrides the viewport max and overflows narrow windows. The chosen composition provides a normal baseline, grows for larger content, shrinks within the viewport, and preserves explicit panel_size (Auto restores the baseline). No T517 structural redesign included.

Approved splits: Length and Layout moved out of style.rs with existing public paths re-exported; all 13 original Dialog tests preserved in dialog/tests.rs and dialog/tab_repro.rs, production module now under 600 lines. New sizing tests in dialog/sizing_tests.rs. docs/layout.md, docs/widgets.md and rustdoc updated.

Verification: scoped pre/post cargo check; cargo clippy -p heca-grid-ui -p heca-view -p heca-view-realize --all-targets -- -D warnings clean. Full library/SDK/realizer suites: 965 passed, zero failed, 82 ignored. Tests cover short confirmation baseline, larger rename input, repeated font changes, inherited size variants, narrow/wide resizing, explicit panel size, all length-bearing style fields, native/described layout equality and serde preserving em. Both removed-fix sabotage runs failed as expected, then original code was restored and the complete suites passed.

Application validation: direct heca tests in the current dirty worktree cannot compile because the pre-existing pane_header/segments.rs edit changes triples to quadruples without matching consumers. That file was untouched. In an isolated clean checkout of the same HEAD plus exactly these 12 T286 files, heca suites passed: 896 passed, zero failed, 15 ignored. The temporary verification checkout was inspected and removed; logs remain under target/t286-*.log.

Showcase build passed; catalog sweep passed with RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 (default test stack overflowed). Live showcase rich Delete pane dialog opened, rendered within the window, and Cancel dismissed it. Standalone heca delete/rename GUI flows were not manually exercised; those sizing shapes are covered headlessly. cargo doc succeeds, with existing unrelated warnings outside touched modules. No implementation work remains for this task. No cargo fmt, unrelated code repair, commit or push.

tasks.title: A proportional share must not be written as a fixed measure
tasks.description:
CURRENT IMPLEMENTATION — refreshed 2026-10-25, main code HEAD 6e3e6d36

The proportional-share API is already present: LayoutExt::flex(parts) stores Layout.flex, the layout layer resolves the main-axis share, and heca_view::build::Style::flex writes the same serializable flex property. The missing flex_basis primitive is also delivered. Do not add a second share builder or reimplement either capability.

The old expose share_v/with_share helper is absent; current expose components use .flex(..). A source search found the literal grow/basis/shrink share recipe only in library documentation comments, not in the old app helper. Refresh the complete call-site sweep before concluding all migration acceptance is met.

Verification run during this investigation: cargo test -p heca-grid-ui --test fr_share -- --test-threads=1 passed 4 measured layout tests; cargo test -p heca-view-realize --lib a_described_node_takes_its_parts_with_flex -- --test-threads=1 passed the native/described flex-property test. This is headless evidence, not visual acceptance.

Remaining closeout: reconcile documentation still recommending grow(...).basis(0).shrink(1) as the ordinary way to take a share, verify the complete original share/minimum/overflow/call-site criteria against the delivered .flex API, and record any actual residual instead of creating another implementation. Keep current state planned until that verification is complete.

HISTORICAL FINDINGS AND ACCEPTANCE (the old assertions that flex_basis is absent describe the original investigation, not the current checkout)

# The problem

To make two containers take half a region each, `with_share` (`heca/src/chrome/mod.rs`) writes:

```rust
layout.flex_grow = grow;
layout.height = heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0);      // ← a FIXED measure
layout.min_height = Some(heca_grid_ui::Length::Px(0.0));
layout.flex_shrink = Some(1.0);
```

**A proportional share is being expressed by writing a fixed number**, which is what the user does not
want anyone doing (2026-07-28: *"I don't want other developers to write fixed measure"*). Worse, it is
three coupled fields whose combination is folklore: get one wrong and the split silently reverts to
content-sizing, which is exactly the bug it was written to fix.

# Why it is there

`flex_grow` distributes only **positive free space**. Container content is routinely taller than a
sidebar, so there is no positive free space to distribute — measured 2026-07-28: two containers took
**1214px each inside a 600px body** and divided nothing. In CSS the answer is `flex: 1 1 0`; the base
size of 0 is what makes the whole region free space. With it: **296px each**, measured.

**`Layout` has no `flex_basis`** (confirmed — `grep flex_basis heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs` is empty),
so `height = Px(0)` is standing in for it. taffy *does* have `flex_basis` in its `Style`, so the
concept is available one layer down and simply was never surfaced.

# What to build

1. **Add `flex_basis: Option<Length>` to `Layout`** and map it in `to_taffy`
   (`heca-grid-ui/src/style.rs`). That is the missing word in the vocabulary; everything below already
   understands it.
2. **Give the library one way to say "take a share"** so no caller assembles the trio by hand — a
   builder on `LayoutExt` (`heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs`), e.g. `share(n)`, meaning *n shares of the
   parent's main axis*, setting grow + basis 0 + min 0 + shrink internally. Then:
   - `with_share` becomes one call and stops naming a measure;
   - the SDK's `Style` trait (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) exposes the same thing, so a **described** tree
     can say it too — today it can only set `flex_grow`, which has the same trap;
   - `grow()` stays as the raw flex knob for callers who genuinely want content-based basis.
   Decide whether `grow()` should be *renamed* or documented as the low-level one, so the obvious name
   is the one that behaves as expected.
3. **Main-axis, not height.** `flex_basis` is main-axis relative like `flex_grow`, so one setter covers
   a column and a row (the same reason `ContainerContribution::grow` is not called `height_grow`). Do
   not add a per-axis variant.
4. **Sweep for the same folklore elsewhere.** `ScrollRegion::new()` already sets `min_height: 0` and
   `flex_shrink: 1` by hand with a long comment explaining why (`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/scroll_region.rs:274`).
   Check whether that is the same idea written a second way, and whether it should go through the new
   setter.
5. **Tests must measure, not inspect flags.** A test asserting `flex_grow == 1.0` passed while the
   layout was visibly broken (2026-07-28) — the measured-height test is what caught it. Assert
   pixels: two shares of a 600px region are ~296 each, with content far taller than either.

# Acceptance

- No caller writes a fixed measure to express a proportion — not in `heca`, not in the SDK, not in a
  described tree.
- One setter, documented, with the trio behind it.
- `docs/widgets.md` says how to take a share, next to R8 (the stretch contract) in
  `docs/chrome-and-ui.md` — the two rules are read together.
- Whole workspace green, clippy 0 warnings.
tasks.notes:
PARTLY LANDED 2026-09-16, uncommitted on feat/hint-collapses-to-the-tree.

THIS TASK PREDICTED A REAL DEFECT AND IT HAPPENED. The "three coupled fields whose combination is folklore" (flex_grow + height: Px(0) + min_height + flex_shrink) were still being written by hand in the exposé's share_v, and the zero HEIGHT half of it was the wrong spelling: a definite zero height says "this box is zero", which is a different answer to anything measuring the container's content than "start from nothing, then take your weight".

WHAT LANDED
- heca-grid-ui gained the property that was missing: LayoutExt::basis(..) → Style::Layout::flex_basis → taffy flex_basis. CSS flex-basis, taking pixels, a percentage or "auto". It is a Layout field, so it travels on the wire with no name table to extend.
- A share is now written .grow(w).basis(0.0).shrink(1.0) — literally CSS `flex: 1 1 0`. heca/src/chrome/expose/mod.rs::share_v uses it, and the comment that apologised for spelling it with a zero height is gone.
- Guard: a_share_divides_the_whole_box_by_weight_not_just_the_leftover (heca-grid-ui/src/builders.rs). It took two attempts — the first passed with the mapping deleted and therefore proved nothing, because grow alone divides free space correctly in a simple box. The rewritten one gives the two items DIFFERENT CONTENT, which is where the basis bites: asked for 2:1 in a 900px box, a zero basis gives 600/300 and an auto basis gives 606/294, skewed by what each item started from. Sabotaged, it fails on exactly that.

WHAT IS LEFT, and it is the original scope
- `with_share` in heca/src/chrome/mod.rs still writes the four fields by hand. It is the function this task was opened about; share_v was its twin in the exposé. It should call .basis(0.0) too, or better, be deleted in favour of one shared builder.
- The larger question this task asks — "a proportional share must not be written as a fixed measure" — is answerable now that basis exists. A share is three builders; consider whether it should be ONE (`.share(w)`), so the combination stops being folklore a caller has to remember at all.

RELATED, same day: docs/layout.md now documents the share idiom, each of the three parts, and what each alone does instead.
